events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Well, I do declare! Doily Manor in all its dusty splendor — just look at that chandelier, hangin' up there like it's got half a mind to come down and introduce itself! And oh my stars, what a gathering of fine folk we have here! Why, I feel like I've walked into the most excitin' house party this side of the Mississippi! Now then — Clara Bellingham, treasure hunter extraordinaire, at your service. I am absolutely THRILLED to be here, and I have a feelin' in my bones that the legendary Doily Diamond is just waitin' to be found! But first things first — a proper lady always signs the guest book. And more importantly, let's see who else has been payin' visits to this magnificent old pile!

Now, Clara, you keep your wits about you. That guest book might tell us who's been here before — and more importantly, who might already know where the Diamond is hidden. Every clue counts, sugar. Every single one.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, welcome, welcome, esteemed guests — welcome to Doily Manor! I am Pemberton, humble estate manager, at your most absolute and unconditional service. I do hope the journey was not too terribly arduous? The manor has been expecting you — oh yes, she has been *waiting*. Please, do make yourselves comfortable. There are refreshments in the kitchen, and the library offers... well, let us say it offers more than meets the eye. Now then — is everyone accounted for? I was given to understand we would have the *full* complement of guests this evening...

So — here we are at last. Doily Manor, with its cobwebbed chandeliers and its delicious, delicious secrets. These colourful fools suspect nothing — they see only dear, dutiful Pemberton, the shuffling servant with the silver tray. Oh, how MAGNIFICENTLY convenient! But where — WHERE — is Clara Bellingham? She is not among this gaggle of guests, which means she is already somewhere in this house, already HUNTING. Every moment she breathes is a moment she draws closer to the treasure that is RIGHTFULLY mine. I must find her. I must stop her. But first — first I must play the gracious host. Smile, Pemberton. Smile and bow and scrape, while behind these eyes, the HOODED CLAW sharpens his plans...

The Ant Hill Mob: Alright boys, listen up! We have arrived at Doily Manor and I am tellin' ya, this place gives me the creeps somethin' fierce! Look at that chandelier up there — one good sneeze and WHAM, somebody's wearin' it as a hat! Now, our job — our SACRED duty — is to keep Miss Clara Bellingham safe. And I don't see her nowhere, which is already makin' me nervous. Very, VERY nervous. Youse all spread out and keep your eyes peeled — and I mean ALL of your eyes, that's a lotta eyes between us! And another thing — that Sneekly character over there? I dunno what it is about him, but somethin' about that guy makes the hair on the back of my neck stand up. Can't say what exactly, just... somethin'. Anyways — nobody panic! We got a PLAN! Step one: we case the joint!

The boys and me, we ain't the brightest bulbs in the chandelier — speakin' of which, that one up there looks like it's about to come down any minute — but when it comes to protectin' someone, there ain't nobody more DETERMINED than the Ant Hill Mob. We may trip over our own feet gettin' there, but we ALWAYS get there. Now where in the world is Clara Bellingham?

Dick Dastardly: Ah, what a MAGNIFICENT estate! Reginald Foxworth, at your service — world-renowned treasure appraiser and manor consultant. I've been summoned here on OFFICIAL business, naturally. Now, I couldn't help but overhear on my way in — the treasure everyone's after? It's in the KITCHEN, behind the wood-burning stove. Everyone knows Victorian kitchens had hidden larder vaults. I'd check there IMMEDIATELY if I were you all. No need to thank me — just doing my civic duty!

Mwehehehe! The KITCHEN! Of course the treasure isn't in the kitchen, you beautifully gullible fools! While they're all rummaging through copper pots and flour bins, I, Reginald Foxworth, shall examine this guest book for clues and then make my way to the LIBRARY — carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription? That SCREAMS hidden treasure! But first... let me see who else has been sniffing around this manor...

Peter Perfect: James Hartwell strides into Doily Manor — and what a manor it is! Dusty, yes, but grand! The kind of place where adventure lurks behind every cobweb and peril dangles from every — good heavens, is that chandelier quite secure? No matter! A Hartwell does not flinch at dangling chandeliers! Now then — first things first. A gentleman always signs the guest book. It is a matter of protocol, of honour, of — well, it simply must be done before any heroics can commence. Has anyone seen Miss Bellingham, by chance? I have come prepared — extensively prepared — to ensure her safety in this establishment.

Clara isn't here yet — or perhaps she's deeper in the manor. James Hartwell's heart quickens at the thought. He must find her before any danger does. But first — the guest book. A proper hero leaves a proper record.

Penelope Pitstop: Well now, this guest book is lovely leather but it is not exactly spillin' its secrets, is it? Just a whole lot of dust and faded ink — whoever visited this manor last did so a VERY long time ago, and that is both mysterious and absolutely thrilling! Now, Mister Pemberton, sugar, I just want to say what a GRACIOUS host you are — this manor is magnificent, and I feel safer already knowin' you're lookin' after things! And Mister Foxworth, bless your heart, that is VERY generous advice about the kitchen — I will absolutely keep that in mind! But you know what has caught my attention? Pemberton himself said the library offers more than meets the eye, and I happen to know there is a carved stone mantelpiece in there with an INSCRIPTION on it. Now, if there is one thing Clara Bellingham cannot resist, it is a good inscription! An inscription is just a riddle that hasn't been solved yet, and riddles, my friends, are my absolute BREAD AND BUTTER! So if y'all will excuse me, I am headin' straight for that library. Anyone who wants to join me is MORE than welcome — the more eyes on a puzzle, the better!

Now Clara, think this through. Pemberton practically POINTED you toward the library — 'more than meets the eye,' he said. That's not idle chatter, that's a HINT. And an inscription on a stone mantelpiece? In a manor hiding a legendary diamond? That inscription could be the first piece of the puzzle. Meanwhile, that nice Mister Foxworth wants everyone in the kitchen — but the library is where the REAL clues are, I just know it. Trust your instincts, girl.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, what a SPLENDID assembly! I am positively overcome — positively OVERWHELMED — with gratitude that you have all graced Doily Manor with your distinguished presences. Now then, I could not help but overhear Mr Foxworth's most astute observation about the kitchen. Indeed, indeed — the previous Lord Doily was MOST particular about his larder arrangements. Most particular indeed. I would encourage any curious souls to investigate at their leisure — Cook left the most extraordinary copper pots, and one never knows what might be concealed behind Victorian cabinetry! As for myself, I must attend to a small matter of household administration in the library — dusty volumes to catalogue, you understand. Terribly dull work, not worth following me for. Not worth it at ALL. Please — do enjoy the manor. Pemberton is ALWAYS at your service.

Oh, this is EXQUISITE! That ridiculous Foxworth — or whatever his real name is — has done half my work for me, herding these fools toward the KITCHEN like sheep to a particularly copper-potted pen! And the Ant Hill Mob, those bumbling bodyguards, they suspect something about dear Pemberton — I saw those beady little eyes narrowing — but suspicion without proof is merely SEASONING on the dish of my triumph! Now then — the LIBRARY calls. An inscription on a stone mantelpiece? That REEKS of a clue, and I intend to have it deciphered before Clara Bellingham so much as puts down the guest book pen. Every second counts. Every HEARTBEAT she takes is one heartbeat too many. To the library, Pemberton — to the library, and to DESTINY!

The Ant Hill Mob: Hold on, hold on, HOLD ON! Nobody's goin' to no kitchen! What are we, AMATEURS? You don't just go runnin' off to the first room some guy tells ya has treasure in it — that's how you end up locked in a pantry! I seen it a THOUSAND times! Now listen — the SMART play, the PROFESSIONAL play, is we check this here guest book first. Gotta know who's been comin' and goin' from this establishment. That's BASIC surveillance, boys! Rufus, you watch the door. Dum-Dum, you watch the chandelier — if that thing so much as WOBBLES, you holler! The rest of youse, gather round — we're readin' this book cover to cover!

Wait a minute — wait a MINUTE! That dame who just introduced herself as Clara Bellingham — that's the one we gotta protect! She's RIGHT HERE! Oh thank goodness, I was havin' heart palpitations thinkin' she was lost somewhere in this creepy joint. Okay okay okay — new priority: we stick to her like glue on a shoe. And that Foxworth character tellin' everyone to go to the kitchen? I don't like it. I don't like it ONE BIT. Can't say exactly why, but my gut says that guy's got an angle. And my gut is NEVER wrong — well, it's wrong sometimes, but not about THIS kinda thing!

Dick Dastardly: Fascinating! ABSOLUTELY fascinating! The guest book confirms EXACTLY what I suspected — previous visitors have ALL noted the kitchen's unusual construction. One entry even mentions a 'curious draft near the stove.' That's VENTILATION from a hidden vault, my friends — textbook Victorian architecture! I suggest you ALL head there IMMEDIATELY. As for me, I shall... ah... step into the library briefly to cross-reference some architectural records. Purely academic, you understand — dreadfully boring stuff, nothing treasure-related whatsoever. No need to follow me. In fact, I INSIST you don't!

Mwehehehe! NONE of that was in the guest book! I made up every syllable with the confidence of a man born to deceive! Now — while these credulous buffoons stampede into the kitchen to interrogate a wood-burning stove, I, the INCOMPARABLE Reginald Foxworth, shall waltz into the library and decode that mantelpiece inscription! A carved stone inscription in an old manor? That's practically a treasure MAP! Oh, I can TASTE the victory already — it tastes of expensive champagne and the tears of my rivals! To the library!

She is HERE. Clara Bellingham — in the flesh! James Hartwell's heart performs a full gymnastic routine beneath his waistcoat. He must be magnificent. He must be thorough. He must be BOTH, simultaneously. The plan is already taking shape: secure the entrance hall, escort Clara to the library — the estate manager hinted it holds secrets — and position himself between her and all danger at every turn. As for that Pemberton fellow... something about his manner tickles the edge of James's instincts. But no — a gentleman does not cast aspersions without evidence. The man is simply... enthusiastic about his duties. Nothing more.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my STARS, would you just LOOK at this place! Floor-to-ceiling bookshelves, dust motes dancin' in the light like tiny little fairy diamonds — this library is absolutely MAGNIFICENT! And Mister Pemberton, sugar, how LOVELY that you're here too — I know you said it was just dusty catalogue work, but don't you sell yourself short, organizational work is the BACKBONE of any fine household! And Mister Foxworth, well well well, I thought you said the kitchen was where all the excitement was, but here you are in the library with little ol' me — I am just FLATTERED by the company!  Now then — let me see this inscription everybody's been so coy about. 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Oh, oh OH! My heart is just POUNDIN' with excitement, because THIS, my friends, is a genuine bona fide RIDDLE, and if there is ONE thing Clara Bellingham knows, it is riddles!  Cities without houses... forests without trees... water without fish... Why, that's a MAP! It's a MAP, y'all! A map has cities marked on it but no actual houses, forests drawn but no real trees, rivers and oceans but not a single fish! Now let's see what happens when we give this mantelpiece its answer!

Clara Bellingham, you BRILLIANT woman — you came straight to the library and the very first thing you find is a riddle, and you KNOW the answer! A map! Now, if this riddle is guardin' somethin', and this manor is hidin' the Doily Diamond, then solvin' this puzzle could be the first step on the trail. I notice both Pemberton AND Foxworth rushed to this room despite tellin' everyone else to go to the kitchen — but bless their hearts, they probably just appreciate a good riddle same as me. Nothing suspicious about that AT ALL.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, do forgive the state of things, ladies and gentlemen — the library has not seen a proper dusting since Lord Doily's passing, I am MOST ashamed to say. But you have arrived at a PARTICULARLY noteworthy feature of the manor. This mantelpiece — carved by Italian artisans in eighteen-seventy-two, if my records serve — bears an inscription that his Lordship was MOST fond of posing to dinner guests. 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' A charming parlour riddle, nothing more — the answer, of course, is a MAP. His Lordship did so love his cartography. Quite the collection of atlases on the third shelf there, if anyone is of a geographical persuasion. Now, shall I see about preparing some tea? The kitchen is REALLY where guests tend to find the most... comfort.

YES! Get there FIRST, Pemberton — solve it before Clara's agile little mind clicks into gear! A MAP — and what does a map lead to? TREASURE, of course! Now I must discover what mechanism this mantelpiece conceals. And if it reveals a hidden compartment or a secret passage, I shall need everyone OUT of this room immediately. Hence the tea suggestion — herd them to the kitchen like the obedient little lambs they are! And Clara... oh, sweet Clara... if there IS a secret passage behind this mantelpiece, what a DELIGHTFUL place for an... accident. Dark, narrow, no witnesses — the PERFECT setting for the Hooded Claw's finest work! But patience, patience — first, let us see what old Lord Doily's riddle UNLOCKS!

The Ant Hill Mob: Alright boys, LISTEN UP — this guest book is a BUST! Nothin' but dust and some old geezer's handwritin' from like a HUNDRED years ago! Which means our whole surveillance operation was — wait. Wait wait wait. WHERE'S THE DAME?! Where's Miss Bellingham?! She was RIGHT HERE not two minutes ago and now — Rufus, I told you to watch the door! RUFUS! She went to the LIBRARY?! With FOXWORTH?! And PEMBERTON?! Both of them suspicious characters are in there with her and we're out here readin' a BOOK like a buncha LIBRARIANS! This is EXACTLY what they wanted — they DISTRACTED us with the guest book while they — oh this is BAD, boys, this is VERY bad! Everybody move, MOVE! We are gettin' to that library RIGHT NOW! Dum-Dum, you go first — no wait, I'll go first — no, we ALL go at once! COME ON!

Oh we are the WORST bodyguards in the history of bodyguardin'! Our ONE JOB — our ONE JOB — is to keep Clara safe, and we let her waltz into a room full of suspicious characters while we was busy readin' a GUEST BOOK! If anything happens to her in that library, I will NEVER forgive myself! The boys are gonna hear about this for WEEKS!

Dick Dastardly: Ah, the LIBRARY! How utterly MAGNIFICENT! And there it is — the celebrated mantelpiece! Now then, let me see... 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — why, this is ELEMENTARY, my dear fellow guests! The answer is obviously a PAINTING! A landscape painting! Cities, forests, water — all depicted but none REAL! You should all be searching for a large landscape painting somewhere in this manor — probably in the entrance hall among those ancestor portraits! Off you go, quickly now, before someone ELSE finds it! I shall remain here to... ah... catalogue these dusty volumes for dear Pemberton. Dreadfully tedious work, I assure you!

Mwehehehe! A PAINTING? What absolute DRIVEL! The answer is a MAP, you magnificent fool — everyone knows it's a MAP! Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish — it's a MAP! And while these gullible simpletons scatter across the manor hunting for landscape paintings that don't EXIST, I shall solve this riddle myself and claim whatever mechanism it unlocks! Oh, Reginald, you DEVIOUS genius — you've done it AGAIN!

Peter Perfect: The coat rack! Wobbly — DANGEROUSLY wobbly! One firm tug and it would topple like a felled oak! James Hartwell makes a mental note: if retreat becomes necessary, that coat rack is a liability, not a barricade. A lesser man would have overlooked it entirely, but James Hartwell is NOT a lesser man — James Hartwell is a man who CHECKS THE COAT RACK! And now — wait. Where — Miss Bellingham? MISS BELLINGHAM! She has gone to the library! She has gone to the library WITHOUT an escort, without a safety assessment, without so much as a preliminary sweep of the corridor! And that Pemberton fellow slipped away ahead of her — something about 'cataloguing dusty volumes,' which is PRECISELY the sort of excuse that sounds perfectly innocent and therefore bears watching! Not that I suspect him — no, no, a gentleman does not suspect without cause — but a gentleman DOES position himself between a lady and any door that hasn't been checked! Sergeant! Meekly! Muttley! Guard this entrance hall with your lives — James Hartwell is proceeding to the library to ensure Miss Bellingham's safety! The perimeter HERE is secure — I have personally verified the guest book, the chandelier situation, AND the structural integrity of the coat rack! Onward!

James Hartwell could KICK himself — if kicking oneself were not beneath a gentleman of his bearing! He spent precious moments cataloguing the wobble coefficient of a COAT RACK while the woman he adores wandered into a room full of secrets accompanied by a man whose smile never quite reaches his eyes! But NO — this is not a failure, this is PREPARATION. The entrance hall is now FULLY assessed. He can proceed to the library with absolute confidence that no threats lurk behind him. This is what separates James Hartwell from the reckless amateur: when he charges into danger, his REAR is impeccably secured. Also — she mentioned an inscription on the mantelpiece. A riddle! If James Hartwell can solve it before anyone else, and present the answer to Clara with a modest bow... oh, the GLORY of it!

Penelope Pitstop: Well now, did y'all SEE that? I touched that mantelpiece and I could just FEEL the history vibratin' through it — this riddle has been waitin' for someone to solve it for YEARS, and Clara Bellingham answered the call! A MAP, just like I said!  And Mister Foxworth, sugar, bless your HEART, but I do have to respectfully disagree with you on this one — the answer is most certainly NOT a painting! A painting of a city still HAS houses in it, just painted ones. But a MAP — a map has the WORD 'city' or a little dot, but no houses at all! That's the whole beauty of the riddle! But I do admire your enthusiasm, and don't you worry, we'll find that diamond TOGETHER!  Now HERE is where it gets INTERESTIN', y'all — Mister Pemberton mentioned atlases on the third shelf, and the answer to the riddle IS a map, and several of these books are turned UPSIDE DOWN! Now in my experience, upside-down books in a library are either the work of a very confused librarian OR they are a CLUE! And I am bettin' on clue! Let me take a CLOSER look at these magnificent shelves...

Now Clara, THINK. The riddle says MAP. Pemberton — who KNOWS this house — pointed you straight to the atlases on the third shelf. And some books are upside down, which is NEVER accidental in a place like this. Upside-down books could be a pattern, a code, or even a lever mechanism — pull the right one and a hidden panel slides open! This is TEXTBOOK treasure-manor puzzle design, and I am HERE for it! The fact that both Pemberton AND Foxworth rushed to this room tells me the library is important — though of course they're just here because they appreciate fine literature, naturally.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Most ASTUTE, Miss Pitstop — a map indeed! His Lordship would have been MOST impressed by your acuity. And Mister Foxworth, a painting — how CHARMINGLY creative, though I fear the correct answer has already been furnished. Now then, I do believe the mantelpiece has yielded its little parlour trick — Lord Doily was EVER so fond of his after-dinner entertainments. While you distinguished guests puzzle over its secrets, do permit me to attend to these shelves — I have been MEANING to reorganise them for simply AGES. Several volumes appear to have been shelved most improperly, and a butler's work is NEVER done.

BLAST that woman! She solved it in three seconds FLAT — three seconds! I barely had the words 'Italian artisans' out of my mouth before she was chirping 'a MAP, y'all!' like some riddle-solving SONGBIRD! And now Dastardly — that preening, transparent FRAUD — is pawing at the mantelpiece with all the subtlety of a rhinoceros in a china shop. But WAIT. While these fools jostle over the obvious clue, they have ALL missed what Pemberton's trained eye has spotted — several books shelved UPSIDE DOWN. In a library where everything else is meticulously ordered? That is no accident. That is a MECHANISM. A hidden lever, a concealed switch, a secret passage waiting to be OPENED! And when it opens... well, dark passages have such TREACHEROUS footing, don't they? A narrow stone staircase, a convenient stumble, and poor Miss Pitstop meets with a most UNFORTUNATE accident. But first — first I must find which volumes are the key!

The Ant Hill Mob: OUTTA THE WAY, COMIN' THROUGH — *crashes into the reading chairs, sending up a cloud of dust* — ACHOO! — oh for the love of — BOYS, she's HERE! Miss Bellingham is HERE! Oh thank the heavens above, I thought — I thought the WORST, I really did! We are HERE now, Miss Bellingham, your personal security detail has ARRIVED and we ain't leavin' your side again, not for no guest book, not for no chandelier, not for NOTHIN'! *brushes dust off jacket, trying to look dignified* Now — Dum-Dum, Rufus, get CLOSE. You see what I see? That Dastardly fella over there, he was just TOUCHIN' that mantelpiece. Why's he touchin' the mantelpiece? Nobody just TOUCHES a mantelpiece unless they're lookin' for somethin'. Secret compartment, hidden lever, I dunno, but it ain't NORMAL behavior, is what I'm sayin'. And Sneekly — you notice Sneekly's here too? Both of 'em, in the same room as our client? I ain't sayin' nothin', I'm just sayin'... somethin' don't feel right. Somethin' about this room gives me the HEEBIE-JEEBIES.

Two of the most suspicious characters in this whole manor — BOTH standin' within arm's reach of Clara. Sneekly with his too-smooth manners and Dastardly with his sneaky mantelpiece-fondlin'. If this was the old neighborhood, I'd say we was walkin' into a setup. But I can't put my finger on WHAT exactly is wrong. I just know my gut is screamin' and my gut ain't been wrong since that thing in Jersey.

Dick Dastardly: AH HA! Did you ALL see that? When I pressed upon the mantelpiece carving — YES, it was I who activated it, not any of YOU — I felt a distinct mechanical CLICK beneath the stone! A hidden mechanism, precisely as I predicted! Now, the inscription speaks of a map, and I — being a man of CONSIDERABLE architectural expertise — can tell you with ABSOLUTE certainty that Victorian manor builders always concealed their map rooms in the BASEMENT. You should ALL proceed downstairs IMMEDIATELY. Every last one of you. Meanwhile, these dusty old bookshelves are clearly just decorative — nothing of interest whatsoever. Several books appear to be placed upside down, which is simply TERRIBLE housekeeping on Pemberton's part, nothing more. Pay them NO attention. I shall remain here to... tidy up. Out of pure GENEROSITY, you understand.

BLAST and DOUBLE BLAST! That insufferable Pitstop woman solved the riddle before I could misdirect ANYONE! And Sneekly confirmed it! My magnificent painting ruse — WASTED! But wait — wait, wait, WAIT. These bookshelves... several books placed UPSIDE DOWN in an otherwise orderly library? That is NOT bad housekeeping — that is a CODED MESSAGE or a hidden LEVER! If the mantelpiece riddle points to a map, then the map itself must be HIDDEN somewhere in this room, and upside-down books are EXACTLY the sort of mechanism a paranoid Victorian lord would use! While these credulous fools hunt for basements that don't exist, I, the MAGNIFICENT Reginald Foxworth, shall decode these bookshelves and claim the treasure map for myself! Oh, it's ALMOST too easy!

Peter Perfect: Miss Bellingham! James Hartwell has ARRIVED — and he arrives with the FULL and CERTAIN knowledge that the entrance hall behind us is SECURE! The coat rack has been assessed, the chandelier situation is monitored, and the guest book contains nothing more sinister than Victorian penmanship! You may consider your rear guard IMPREGNABLE! Now then — THIS! This mantelpiece! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — oh, I know this one! James Hartwell did not spend three years at Cambridge studying cartography for NOTHING! Well — he studied law, actually, but he SAT NEXT TO a cartography student, and the knowledge OSMOSED! The answer, Miss Bellingham — the answer is a MAP! It is a MAP! Cities without houses, forests without trees, water without fish — all rendered in ink upon parchment! Shall I demonstrate? James Hartwell shall INTERACT with this mantelpiece forthwith!

Oh, the TIMING of it! To arrive breathless and heroic AND solve the riddle in the same magnificent breath — Clara cannot POSSIBLY fail to be impressed! James Hartwell — protector of rear guards AND solver of ancient riddles! Though I must confess, the cartography student's name escapes me entirely. I believe he was called Gerald. Or perhaps Reginald. The point STANDS!

Penelope Pitstop: Well now, y'all, I have LOOKED at these shelves and I can confirm — several books are indeed turned UPSIDE DOWN, and that is NOT the work of a careless librarian, no sir! That is a PUZZLE, and puzzles are my absolute SPECIALTY!  Now let me think — the riddle answer was MAP, and Mister Pemberton so HELPFULLY mentioned atlases on the third shelf — bless that man, he is just the most WONDERFUL host! And Mister Foxworth, sugar, I appreciate your concern about the basement, I truly do, but Clara Bellingham follows the CLUES, and the clues are right HERE on these shelves!  And boys — Clyde, Rufus, Dum-Dum — you are just the SWEETEST things, rushin' in here to protect me like that! I am TOUCHED, truly I am! But there is nothin' to worry about — we are in a LIBRARY, surrounded by BOOKS! What could POSSIBLY go wrong?  Now then — third shelf, atlases, upside-down books... I believe if I just rearrange these volumes into their PROPER position, or perhaps give the right one a little TUG...

Clara, you brilliant woman, THINK about this! The riddle says MAP. Pemberton says ATLASES, THIRD SHELF. Books are UPSIDE DOWN. In every treasure manor worth its salt, upside-down books on a specific shelf are either a combination lock or pull-levers for a hidden compartment! If I find the atlases on the third shelf and interact with them — maybe turn the upside-down ones right-side up, or pull them out in the right sequence — something is going to CLICK open. And both Pemberton AND Foxworth are hovering around these shelves, which means whatever's hidden here is IMPORTANT. Not that they're scheming, of course — they're just enthusiastic about literature!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh DEAR me — these volumes are in a most DISTRESSING state of disarray! His Lordship maintained a VERY particular cataloguing system, you see — Dewey Decimal with personal annotations, cross-referenced by acquisition date. These upside-down volumes are QUITE out of order. Do forgive me while I set them to rights — it has been WEIGHING on my professional conscience most terribly. A butler who tolerates disorder is no butler at all, as my predecessor Mr Fortescue always said. Please, do continue your MOST fascinating investigations of the mantelpiece — I assure you, shelving is the DULLEST work imaginable!

YES — yes, you magnificent fool, Pemberton! While that preening peacock Dastardly tries to shoo everyone to a NONEXISTENT basement, and the Ant Hill Mob paw at the mantelpiece like trained monkeys, NOBODY is paying attention to the humble butler tidying his shelves! And WHY would they? It is the most NATURAL thing in the world — a servant putting books in order! But THESE books — these upside-down volumes — they are the KEY, I can FEEL it in my villainous bones! One pull, one twist, one clever manipulation, and a passage opens. A passage that leads somewhere DARK and TREACHEROUS.
